clue.text: Politician's annoyed expression about come-back

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: drat is an exclamation of annoyance
the word come read back to front gives EMOC

explanation.surface: A politician mutters crossly about some return to the fray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' is one hyphenated word doing two things: it gives the word come and says to read it backwards. 'about' then wraps the exclamation around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is a politician.

clue.text: Old maid's book of the Italian binding

indicators.note: binding means the Italian words wrap around the book

parts.note: del means of the in Italian
Amos is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A spinster owns a book with an Italian binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old maid' suggests a spinster, but here 'old' marks the archaic word for a maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic spelling of damsel, a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Publication united after change in size

parts.note: a mag is a magazine

indicators.note: after change means the word united, once altered, follows the first piece

explanation.surface: A magazine, newly merged, changes its format.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude means extent or dimensions, how big something is.

clue.text: Invited people connected with King Edward

parts.note: a royal court is the monarch's household and attendants
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Guests linked to King Edward were asked along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks like one monarch, but the words split: the king's people, then Edward alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo or seek out, so courted means invited or solicited.

clue.text: Waterproof gear right in an annual horse-race

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the race name

parts.note: the Oaks is a classic flat race for fillies run each year at Epsom

explanation.surface: Rainwear is the right thing to wear at a yearly race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is one of England's five classic horse races, run at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks are hooded weatherproof jackets.

clue.text: Merlin, say, gives blow to king

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock or blow
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: The wizard Merlin strikes a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Merlin looks like the wizard of Arthurian legend, but here it is the merlin, a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small falcon, an example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Trains one awfully poor horse

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of trains and one are scrambled badly

explanation.surface: A badly trained nag.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is the broken-down horse ridden by Don Quixote in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocinante is Don Quixote's bony old steed, so the name stands for any worn-out nag.

clue.text: Quiet revision required for first examination

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a review is a revision or reassessment

explanation.surface: A silent revision is needed before the first exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'examination' looks like a school test, but the definition is an advance look.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is an advance showing or look before the general view.

clue.text: Enchanting note carried by Oliver Twist, say

indicators.note: carried by means the note is held inside the next word

parts.note: Dickens's Oliver Twist is a parentless boy
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Dickens's foundling carries a charming tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' suggests an anagram, but Oliver Twist is the Dickens hero, an example of an orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphean refers to Orpheus, whose music could charm beasts and stones, so it means melodious and spellbinding.

clue.text: A lot of wine mixed up so in large volume

parts.note: a magnum is a big wine bottle holding two standard bottles

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the following two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lots of wine, carelessly blended, in great quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles UP SO into OPUS; 'in large volume' reads as quantity of wine but 'large volume' is the definition, with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum opus is a writer's great work, often a weighty tome.

clue.text: Spot one's pony skipping on and on

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the named letters are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: the possessive written out as letters, apostrophe ignored
two copies of the word on

explanation.surface: Someone's pony keeps on jumping endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: From ONESPONY take out ON (the first two letters) and ON (in pONy), leaving E, S, P, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a synonym for spot as a verb.

clue.text: Martyr's son isn't a Veronese gentleman

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
Valentine is one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona

explanation.surface: The martyr's son denies being a gentleman from Verona.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona has Valentine and Proteus as its title pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint of 14 February was a Roman priest put to death for his faith.

clue.text: Colour design showing French town

indicators.note: showing means the letters are on display inside the words colour design

explanation.surface: A colour scheme on display in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'coLOUR DESign'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes is a pilgrimage town in the Pyrenees in south-west France.

clue.text: Runner's opponent cut out before our race

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
man means mankind, the human race

explanation.surface: A runner's rival dropped out ahead of our race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a smuggler, or rum-runner; the exciseman was the customs officer who chased them.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman collected duties and pursued smugglers, so was their natural opponent.

clue.text: No point in ruler being informed

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the word for ruler

parts.note: a king is a ruler
taken as written
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A monarch who is quite pointless is well informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point here, W for west.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing means aware or well-informed, as in a knowing look.

clue.text: Differences in the pitch account for breaks

definitions.meaning: the musical gaps between two notes, such as thirds or fifths
pauses, such as the interlude at a theatre or a half-time

explanation.surface: Variations in the playing field explain why play stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but the first sense is musical; 'account for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is both a step between musical notes and a break in a performance.

clue.text: Pope's capital new team includes many churchmen

indicators.note: capital means the capital letter, the first one, of the word Pope's
includes means the team word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a relay is a fresh set of horses or workers taking over from tired ones
C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword convention for many

explanation.surface: The Pope's city fields a fresh side containing lots of clerics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope's capital' looks like Rome, but it is just P, the capital letter of Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelacy means the body of prelates, high-ranking clergy, taken collectively.

clue.text: Deliver an item of news for publication

definitions.meaning: to set free or let go
a press statement handed out to journalists

explanation.surface: Hand over a story for the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release, and a statement issued to the press is a press release.

clue.text: Information makes one doubly depressed

parts.note: low means feeling depressed
down is a second word for depressed

explanation.surface: News that leaves someone twice as miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' asks for two different words each meaning depressed, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowdown is the inside facts on something, slang for the full information.

clue.text: Clergyman retains a source of energy

indicators.note: retains means the clergyman word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A priest keeps hold of some power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is a plant that generates power.

clue.text: Did some Bible reading, say, in Cornwall

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, read past tense sounding like red

parts.note: read Ruth, a book of the Old Testament, with read in the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone studied scripture, perhaps, down in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Past-tense 'read' sounds like 'red'; Redruth is a town in Cornwall, England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: Redruth is an old mining town in Cornwall, so it is a place to be found there.

clue.text: A team that's otherwise gets Rugby Union upset

definitions.text: A team that's otherwise gets Rugby Union upset

indicators.note: that's otherwise means the word team is rearranged
upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: A side playing differently upsets the rugby authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby Union was strictly unpaid when this was set, so a side of non-professionals is its very picture; 'that's otherwise' turns TEAM into MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur plays without pay, as rugby union players then had to.

clue.text: Remains in university, in lodge

indicators.note: the second in means the letter goes inside the lodging word

parts.note: to reside is to lodge or dwell

explanation.surface: Stays at a college, living in.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, a synonym of remains as a noun.

clue.text: Island novelist and boatman

parts.note: Sinclair Lewis or C. S. Lewis, writers of novels
Harris is one of the Three Men in a Boat in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel

explanation.surface: An island, a writer and a man who rows.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis and Harris is the largest island of Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis and Harris is a single landmass in the Western Isles, off north-west Scotland.

clue.text: Tree-ring found in part of Ireland

parts.note: may is another name for hawthorn
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Tree rings found in an Irish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-ring' reads as growth rings in timber, but splits into two pieces: may (hawthorn) and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Watch part Mimi had in opera

definitions.meaning: the longer pointer on a clock face
in La Boheme Rodolfo sings 'Your tiny hand is frozen' to Mimi

explanation.surface: Part of a timepiece that an operatic heroine possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's aria 'Che gelida manina' tells Mimi her tiny hand is cold, so hers was a little hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's long pointer is its minute hand, and minute also means tiny.

clue.text: Standard state cut operating

indicators.note: cut means the state's name is shortened, losing its tail

parts.note: Pennsylvania is a US state, often shortened to Penn
on means working or running

explanation.surface: A national flag cuts operating costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims Pennsylvania to PENN; then add ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, and a standard is a flag or banner.

clue.text: Sort of Jew's harp that's different, I understand

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: that's different means the word harp is rearranged

parts.note: I see is a way of saying I understand

explanation.surface: A Jew's harp is a different kind of instrument, I gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jew's harp' reads as the musical instrument, but the definition ends at 'Jew's'; 'that's different' turns HARP into PHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a strict Jewish sect of the Second Temple period.
